Export and redraw figures

plot-export.Rmd

Save Sankey and Chord diagrams as HTML first. HTML is suitable for inspecting dense connections and deciding which taxa or functions to keep in a static figure. Create the objects using the taxon-to-function or function-to-taxon guide.

Table 1. Figure export formats
Plot type Preview and exploration Static output
PCA, heatmap, error bars, boxplots, dendrograms and signed-effect plots Display the ggplot in R ggplot2::ggsave()
Sankey with taxonomy or phylogeny save_sankey() to HTML SVG, PNG or PDF with save_sankey()
Adjustable Sankey without a tree HTML is required for dragging nodes Keep HTML or save the reusable object as RDS
Chord save_chord() to HTML Filter taxa/functions in R, regenerate the Chord and save a focused PDF

Sankey HTML with a side tree 

save_sankey(p_tax_taxonomy, file.path(out, "sankey_taxonomy.html"))
save_sankey(p_tax_phylogeny, file.path(out, "sankey_phylogeny.html"))
save_sankey(p_tax_taxonomy, file.path(out, "sankey_taxonomy.rds"))

Both taxonomy and phylogeny Sankeys can be saved as HTML. Their side trees use fixed layouts; HTML preserves the supported hover and link inspection behaviour. For a static copy, use save_sankey(p_tax_taxonomy, file.path(out, "sankey_taxonomy.pdf")). Tree PNG/PDF export requires rsvg.

Adjustable Sankey HTML 

p_plain <- tax2fun_sankey(result_taxa, tree_mode = "none")
save_sankey(p_plain, file.path(out, "sankey_adjustable.html"),
            selfcontained = FALSE)

Open the HTML in a browser and drag nodes up or down. The links follow their new positions. Save HTML for this version because a static PDF cannot preserve dragging. Keep the adjacent _files folder with this HTML file. selfcontained = FALSE avoids a Pandoc requirement. Browser adjustments do not automatically update the saved R object or persist after reloading the HTML.

Preview a Chord before exporting PDF 

save_chord(p_tax_chord, file.path(out, "chord_overview.html"))
save_chord(p_tax_chord, file.path(out, "chord_overview.rds"))

A full Chord can contain many sectors and ribbons. Start with HTML to inspect the overview. Large full PDFs can be slow to load. For a taxon-centered figure, choose the taxa in R and regenerate a focused figure for PDF export. For a function-centered figure, choose the functions.

taxa_of_interest <- head(unique(p_tax_chord$links$taxon), 3L)
p_focus <- tax2fun_chord(
  result_taxa, strat_path, ps, group = group_col,
  contrast = c(reference, target),
  taxa_list = taxa_of_interest, max_functions_per_taxon = 10,
  draw = FALSE
)
save_chord(p_focus, file.path(out, "chord_focus.html"))
save_chord(p_focus, file.path(out, "chord_focus.pdf"))

For function-to-taxon Chords, first filter the fitted result list and pass explicit function IDs to fun2tax_chord(). The function-to-taxon guide shows that selection. HTML inspection helps you choose a subset; apply that choice in R before exporting the PDF.

Save ggplots 

ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(out, "boxplot.pdf"), p_tax_box,
                width = 10, height = 6)

Keep the fitted result RDS files, input paths, selected functions, taxonomic rank and group contrast with the figures. These let you return to the same analysis and redraw a different selection later.
